title: Quantization inference profile orchestration and sanity playbook
creator: Aisha Mercado
description: Establish an operational playbook and implementation plan to produce per-model default quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) in the model catalog, plus automated calibration workflows and sanity/rollback guardrails. The deliverable is a curated recommended-profile field in the catalog with an attached calibration artifact, CI gates that validate accuracy/regressions, and runtime fallback chains for safety.
background: We have multiple ad-hoc calibration scripts and experimental quant profiles across repos. Customers expect deterministic defaults in the model catalog to enable cost-saving quantized serving without surprising regressions. Past incidents show small perplexity or F1 regressions can cause user-visible degradations. This work standardizes how a recommended quant profile is chosen, validated, and shipped alongside the model entry.
goals: 1) Define canonical profile schema (precision, per-tensor/per-channel settings, calibration seed artifacts). 2) Implement a reproducible calibration pipeline producing artifacts and metrics. 3) Add CI gates to prevent regressions beyond thresholds. 4) Wire catalog to store recommended profile + fallback chain and expose runtime hints. 5) Create rollout and monitoring playbook with automatic rollback triggers.
success_metrics: - % of catalog models with validated recommended profile >= 70% within 2 quarters. - Average per-token cost reduction across customers using defaults >= 20% for INT8/FP8-backed models. - No customer-facing quality regressions attributed to default profile rollouts in first 3 months. - CI false positives < 5% after calibration refinement.
acceptance_criteria: - Catalog schema extended with 'recommended_quant_profile' and 'calibration_artifact_url'. - Calibration pipeline reproducibly produces artifact and metrics for a model and commits them to artifact storage. - CI job that compares baseline (float32) vs quantized model passes or blocks based on configurable thresholds. - Runtime can route to fallback model/profile automatically when quality or latency constraints fail. - Documentation and runbook published and reviewed by PM and Design.
implementation_notes: We will use the existing calibration harness in infra/quant with standardized dataset sampling and metric hooks. Calibration artifacts will include per-layer scale/zero-point stats, KL histograms, and a small evaluation prompt set. Profiles will include metadata: recommended_precision, per-layer granularity, clipping strategy, calibration_dataset_signature, expected_token_savings, risks.
calibration_workflow_steps: Select representative calibration dataset: sampling policy described (train/dev slices, domain buckets, seed) and fingerprint stored.
Run per-shard activation range estimation with dynamic histogram tracking and per-layer KL divergence computation.
Perform symmetric and asymmetric quant experiments to choose per-layer scheme; prefer per-channel for normalization layers; heuristics encoded in profile chooser.
Run INT8 and FP8 candidate builds through evaluation suite (prompt perplexity, semantic similarity, targeted regression tests).
Compute a delta matrix (metric shifts vs baseline) and a confidence band using bootstrap sampling.
Generate calibration artifact JSON with metadata and upload to artifact storage with a signed URL.
Push candidate profile to validation CI for gating and optionally to shadow rollout for traffic experiments.
Record decisions (why a profile was chosen) as part of the model catalog entry.
If thresholds fail, escalate to manual review with automatic proposed fallback profile (e.g., mixed-precision or per-layer FP16 spots).
validation_tests: Unit: per-layer quant stat reproducibility checks (seeded runs produce identical histograms).
Integration: regression suite comparing generation outputs on canonical prompts; compute semantic similarity (embedding cosine) and perplexity delta.
Load: performance benchmark under representative batching patterns to verify latency and memory improvements claimed by profile.
A/B: small canary with 1% traffic comparing user-visible metrics (latency, errors, quality signals) over 48h.
Safety: run toxic/unsafe prompt battery to ensure quantization does not amplify failure modes; check hallucination markers.
Metric thresholds: default tolerances defined: <= 1.5% perplexity increase OR >= 0.98 semantic-similarity, and no regression in top-k accuracy beyond 0.5% absolute for critical tasks.
CI gating: PRs that change recommended_profile or calibration artifacts must pass the validation CI; otherwise blocked.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal validation — engineering and research validate against owned benchmarks. Duration: 1 week.
Stage 1: Shadow rollout — route production traffic to quantized variant with no user-facing responses; collect metrics for 7 days.
Stage 2: Canary — 1% of traffic, monitor quality and latencies for 48-72 hours with automated checks.
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% guided by metric gates and manual signoff. Typical ramp steps: 1 -> 5 -> 25 -> 100.
Rollback criteria: quality delta exceeds thresholds for 3 consecutive hours, error rates double baseline, or latency SLO breaches persist > 10 minutes.
Post-rollout: 30-day observation window with aggregated alerts and a postmortem sign-off if issues arise.
Communication: automated changelog entry in the model catalog and email to customers on managed tiers when defaults change.
monitoring_and_rollback: Collect token-level latency and cost telemetry; compare expected token savings to realized savings.
Quality monitors: drift detection on eval prompt set using both embedding distance and task-specific metrics.
Automatic fallback: runtime should revert to catalog fallback_profile if drift score exceeds threshold or if tail latency > SLO for 95th percentile.
Alerting: severity-2 on automatic rollback, severity-1 if rollback unable to restore accepted baseline.
Retention: keep calibration artifacts and metric snapshots for 180 days for audit and debugging.
risk_assessment: Risks include silent quality regressions that pass coarse metrics, CI flakiness that blocks valid profile updates, and customer confusion when defaults change. Mitigations: conservative default thresholds, human-in-the-loop approval for models serving regulated customers, richer evaluation sets including adversarial prompts, and robust canary procedures.
migration_steps: For models already in catalog: run batch calibration with a low-risk profile (mixed-precision) and flag candidates. Owners must opt-in for aggressive INT8/FP8 defaults. Provide a migration tool that tags previous profile as 'legacy' and preserves its artifact for rollback.
metrics_and_dashboards: Add per-model dashboard cards: calibration_status, recommended_profile, delta_metrics (perplexity/semantic-similarity), cost_savings_estimate, canary_health. Expose aggregated SLOs for quantized serving and CI gate pass rates.
open_questions: Should we store full calibration histograms in catalog or only a fingerprint + artifact URL (privacy and size trade-offs)?
What is the canonical semantic-similarity metric for diverse tasks (embedding model + threshold) and who signs off on thresholds?
How to best represent mixed-precision profiles in the schema to support runtime routing?
notifications: Will notify customers on dedicated and private tiers via changelog and targeted emails; create a console banner for managed accounts during canary windows.

2026-02-22: Calibration harness patched to expose per-layer KL hist bins; initial INT8 run on bert-large produced 18% token cost reduction with 0.8% perplexity delta.
2026-03-03: CI gating prototype merged to infra:validation; PR link included in references. Observed a flaky semantic-similarity check; debugging flakiness next.
2026-03-10: Shadow rollout started for 'distil-ops-2025' family; monitoring dashboards configured. No user-facing regressions in first 48h.
